title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.19439v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD),

translated_title: 面向小语言模型智能体停滞问题的进度感知蒸馏方法
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体系统在推理和解决复杂现实任务方面已展现出卓越的能力，但同时也伴随着大量的token消耗和推理延迟，限制了其实际部署。为了提升智能体系统的效率，近期的研究工作聚焦于通过基于监督微调的蒸馏方法，将大规模模型的智能体能力迁移到小语言模型（SLM）中。然而，随着交互轨迹的增长，涉及更长的推理-行动链和大量的环境反馈时，经过蒸馏的学生智能体往往会出现进度停滞现象：陷入低效循环，表现为持续失败的策略以及难以取得实质性进展。我们的系统性分析表明，这一现象在多种小语言模型和任务领域中普遍存在。为解决这一问题，我们提出了进度感知蒸馏方法。
tldr: 该论文针对蒸馏得到的小语言模型智能体在长交互轨迹中易陷入低效循环的进度停滞问题，提出了进度感知蒸馏方法予以缓解。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD) to mitigate progress stagnation, where distilled small language model agents get trapped in unproductive loops during long interaction trajectories.
